name: Clyb BDF
plain: A predictor-corrector that uses a faux state at the lower sigma. Every step makes exactly one model call: step 0 calls at σᵢ only, and later steps reuse the prior x0 and call at σ↓. It averages two x0 predictions and then passes them through a scaling function; the projection and default atan2sin modes do not keep that average as-is.
math:
σ↓=√(σᵢ₊₁²/(1+log(1+|σᵢ₊₁−σᵢ|)η)), σ↑=√(σᵢ²−σ↓²).
x̃=lerp(x0₁,x,σ↓/σᵢ); x0₂=model(x̃,σ↓); D=(x0₁+x0₂)/2.
projection: D′=D·(x0₂·D)/D² elementwise. atan2sin: D′=sin(atan x0₂)/cos(atan D). atan2sin+projection (default): both.
x=lerp(D′,x,σ↓/σᵢ). Noise: VP +n·s·σ↑; flow: x=(α_{i+1}/α↓)x+n·s·√(σᵢ₊₁²−σ↓²α²_{i+1}/α↓²). prev x0 := D′.
